speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by understanding the duration and nature of your cough. How many months or years has this been going on, and does it produce any phlegm? If so, what color is it?

speaker: Patient
text: This cough has been sticking around for about two months now. It's mostly dry, but I do notice some clear mucus running down my throat, especially at night. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: Two months is technically subacute, but we must rule out chronic causes. Do you smoke or have you been recently exposed to secondhand smoke or chemical fumes? Also, have you had any recent fevers, night sweats, or weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't smoke, and I haven't been exposed to any smoke or fumes at work. I also haven't had any fevers, night sweats, or lost any weight lately. I want to emphasize that, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: No smoking history and no constitutional symptoms like fever or weight loss make tuberculosis or lung cancer less likely. Have you been exposed to anyone with a cold or flu recently, or do you have a history of allergies and asthma? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray to check for infiltrates or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No acute infiltrates or masses. Normal heart and mediastinal contour.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal chest X-ray results; that effectively rules out pneumonia, lung cancer, and tuberculosis. Have you noticed any wheezing, shortness of breath, or a runny nose that worsens when lying down? Also, does your cough improve temporarily after taking an antihistamine or using a nasal spray?

speaker: Patient
text: I don't feel any wheezing or shortness of breath, but the runny nose definitely gets worse when I lie down. The cough does seem to ease up a bit after I use my nasal spray, but it comes right back later.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-nasal drip syndrome (upper airway cough syndrome) secondary to allergic rhinitis.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Chronic Cough secondary to Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
